group.passage: Every spring, the fishing town of Donggang in Pingtung waits for the season’s first Pacific bluefin tuna. To win the title, a boat registered in Taiwan must be the first to bring a bluefin of at least 175 kilograms back to a local port. In April 2026, a 190-kilogram fish took the honor and sold for a record NT$10,600 per kilogram, over NT$2 million in all. The town has built a festival around the season for about 25 years. The fish deserve the attention. A Pacific bluefin can grow to 4 meters long and 500 kilograms, and each spring many swim into the waters east of Taiwan to lay their eggs. Yet their numbers fell sharply. By 2009 to 2012, overfishing in the late 1990s and the 2000s had cut the stock of adults able to breed to about 2 percent of its natural size. Donggang felt the change early: by 9 May 2003, local boats had caught only 695 bluefin, compared with 1,500 by the same date a year before. The chart shows how much Taiwan’s two groups of tuna longline boats caught over the next twenty years. Rules came next. In 2011, the countries that manage tuna in the western Pacific agreed to take fewer young and adult bluefin, and a similar group in the eastern Pacific followed a year later. Their goal was to rebuild the breeding stock to 20 percent of its natural size by 2034. Taiwan’s boats now share a national quota. In June 2024, when more than 90 percent of it had been used, the Fisheries Agency banned bluefin fishing for the rest of the season. The limits worked faster than expected. The breeding stock passed the 20 percent goal in 2021, more than ten years early, and reached 23.2 percent in 2022. Taiwan’s catch has climbed again as well. The record price paid in Donggang celebrates one big fish, but it also rewards years of patience: fishing less for a time is what made such fish common enough to catch again.

translation_zh.text:
每年春天，屏東的漁港小鎮東港都在等待當季第一尾太平洋黑鮪。要拿到這個頭銜，必須是在臺灣登記的漁船，而且第一個把至少 175 公斤的黑鮪載回本地港口。2026 年 4 月，一尾 190 公斤的黑鮪奪得這份榮耀，以每公斤新臺幣 10,600 元的破紀錄價格賣出，總價超過 200 萬元。這個小鎮圍繞著黑鮪季舉辦活動，已經大約 25 年了。

這種魚值得這樣的關注。太平洋黑鮪可以長到 4 公尺長、500 公斤重，每年春天都有許多黑鮪游進臺灣東部海域產卵。然而，牠們的數量大幅減少。1990 年代末和 2000 年代的過度捕撈，使得到了 2009 至 2012 年間，能繁殖的成魚只剩自然數量的大約 2%。東港很早就感受到這個變化：到 2003 年 5 月 9 日，當地漁船只捕到 695 尾黑鮪，而前一年同一天已經捕到 1,500 尾。圖表顯示接下來二十年間，臺灣兩組鮪延繩釣漁船各捕到多少黑鮪。

接著是規定。2011 年，管理西太平洋鮪類的國家同意少捕年輕與成年的黑鮪，東太平洋的類似組織在隔年跟進。他們的目標是在 2034 年以前，讓可繁殖的族群恢復到自然數量的 20%。臺灣的漁船現在共用一個全國配額。2024 年 6 月，配額已經用掉超過九成時，漁業署就禁止當季剩下的時間再捕黑鮪。

限制的效果比預期來得快。可繁殖的族群在 2021 年就超過 20% 的目標，提早了十年以上，2022 年更達到 23.2%。臺灣的漁獲也再度回升。東港的破紀錄價格慶祝的是一尾大魚，但它也是多年耐心的回報：正是因為有一段時間少捕一些，這樣的大魚才又多到捕得到。

【圖 1】臺灣鮪延繩釣漁船捕獲的太平洋黑鮪（公噸），2003–2023（折線圖）：遠洋漁船從 2003 年的 1482 降到 2012 年的 130，2023 年回升到 1114；近海漁船從 2003 年的 826 降到 2012 年的 80，2023 年回升到 1003；2015–2017 年近海高於遠洋。

open_tasks.prompt: In 2024, Taiwan stopped bluefin fishing once more than 90 percent of the national quota had been used. Do you think a quota is fair to fishermen like those in Donggang? Give your opinion and one reason from the passage in one or two English sentences.
reference_answers: I think a quota is fair, because fishing less for some years helped the bluefin stock pass its goal in 2021, so fishermen can keep catching bluefin in the future.
A quota may feel hard for fishermen in a bad year, but without limits the stock fell to about 2 percent of its natural size, which hurt their catch even more.
